did.abstract: The Daniel Kazimierski Papers include photographs, audio interviews, and moving images created by Daniel Kazimierski in collaboration with veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade. The collection contains a photography project titled For Whom The Bell Tolled (1982-1989), which consists of black and white negatives, photographic prints, an unpublished book mock-up, and audio interviews of Kazimierski's subjects. It also includes Comrades (1987), a 12-minute documentary film about veterans Stanley Postek and Randall "Pete" Smith.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: In the late 1980s, Daniel Kazimierski donated a group of photographic portraits to the Tamiment Library and Robert F. Wagner Archives. The accession number associated with this gift is 1950-289. In 2013, Daniel Kazimierski donated the remainder of materials that he assembled for the photography project, and an additional short documentary film on the same subject. The accession number associated with this gift is 2012-077.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The records are arranged alphabetically by the title of the project, with materials from the same project grouped together.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p: Daniel Kazimierski (1949-) is a Polish American photographer from Warsaw, Poland. He studied photography and film at The Vancouver School of Art, York University, University of Toronto, and New York University.

While studying at New York University, Kazimierski completed two projects in collaboration with veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade: For Whom the Bell Tolled, a photography project that was exhibited at York University in Toronto (1988) and Drew University in Madison, New Jersey (1989); and Comrades, a documentary film that was completed in 1987 and screened at New York University.

prefercite.p: Suggested format for citing materials in a collection:
Identification of item, date; Daniel Kazimierski Papers; ALBA 312; box number; folder number or item identifier; Tamiment Library and Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives, New York University.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: When the Tamiment Library received Daniel Kazimierski's original donation in the late 1980s, the materials were incorporated into the Tamiment Library Labor and Radicalism Photographs Collection (then titled "General Photographs Collection"), PHOTOS 001. In 2013, when Kazimierski donated additional materials, this first group of materials was removed from PHOTOS 001 and incorporated into the Daniel Kazimierski Abraham Lincoln Brigade Veterans Audiovisual Collection (ALBA.MIXED.AUDIO VISUALS.001).

In October 2026, the Daniel Kazimierski Abraham Lincoln Brigade Veterans Audiovisual Collection, ALBA.MIXED.AUDIOVISUALS.001, was retitled the Daniel Kazimierski Papers and given a new call number, ALBA.312. The collection was then arranged and described by an archivist. Paper materials and photographs were placed in acid-free folders in manuscript boxes and oversized materials were foldered and housed appropriately according to their size. Audiovisual materials were placed in format-appropriate housing.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Daniel Kazimierski Papers include photographs, audio interviews, and moving images created by Daniel Kazimierski in collaboration with veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade. The collection contains work from two projects that Kazimierski completed during his studies at New York University, For Whom the Bell Tolled and Comrades.

For Whom The Bell Tolled is a photography project completed in 1982-1984 that depicts veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade. This collection contains black and white negatives, photographic prints, an unpublished book mock-up, and audio interviews of Kazimierski's subjects. While the book was never published, the mock-up was reproduced and displayed at an exhibit titled "For Whom the Bell Tolled" at York University in Toronto (1988), and at Drew University in Madison, New Jersey (1989). Veterans represented in the project include Hy Wallach, Irving Weissman, Joe Brandt, Joe Whelan, Court Bevensee, Randall R. "Pete" Smith, Leonard Lamb, Matti Matson, Albert Coslow, Leonora Temple, Barney Brostoff, Saul Newton, Ben Goldring, Lawrence O'Toole, Edward "Frenchy" Robinson, James Yates, John Simon, Bill Van Felix, Abe Smorodin, Luis Lefkowitz, Moe Fishman, and Ken Graeber.

Comrades is a 12-minute documentary film about Abraham Lincoln Brigade veterans Stanley Postek and Randall "Pete" Smith. After its completion in 1987, the film was screened at New York University. This collection includes a 16mm print of the film, as well as written notes and audio recordings created during production.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Any rights (including copyright and related rights to publicity and privacy) held by Daniel Kazimierski were transferred to New York University in 2017. Permission to publish or reproduce materials in this collection must be secured from the Tamiment Library and Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives. Please contact NYU Special Collections, special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596.

phystech.head: Audiovisual Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Access to some audiovisual materials in this collection is available through digitized access copies. Researchers may view an item's original container, but the media themselves are not available for playback because of preservation concerns. Materials that have already been digitized are noted in the collection's finding aid and can be requested in our reading room.

Audiovisual materials that have not been preserved may not be available to researchers. Materials not yet digitized will need to have access copies made before they can be used. To request an access copy, or if you are unsure if an item has been digitized, please contact NYU Special Collections (special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596) with the collection name, collection number, and a description of the item(s) requested. A staff member will respond to you with further information.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: In October 2026, 1 U-matic tape and 1 DVD-R were deaccessioned after they were found to contain duplicative content.
